can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect continuous to talk about a single activity or state that began in the past and is still continuing, often with 'for' or 'since'.
example_raw:
I've been studying International business there for four years. (Algeria; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Arabic - Meghreb; Pass)

I've been living here since last April and it seemed no problem during spring and summer. (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Japanese; Pass)

Susan has been working in our company for 6 years as a Sales Representative. (Hong Kong; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Action began in past and continues to present
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect continuous for single continuing event with for/since

positives: I have been studying French since I was a child.
She has been living there for three years now.
negatives: I have been to Paris before.
They are studying for their exam.

example_raw:
I hope that I have not been wasting your time and giving you too much trouble. (Malaysia; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Chinese; Pass)

Hope you haven't been working too hard! (Japan; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Japanese; Pass)

The heating system has not been working properly since your staff completed the work in my house. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 2010; Turkish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Denial of a continuing past-to-present action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect continuous in negative form

positives: I haven't been working too hard lately.
The machine has not been running correctly.
negatives: I haven't seen her in a while.
She has been doing her homework.

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect continuous to focus on a finished activity in the recent past but where the effects or results are still important or relevant.
example_raw: They might be slippery when it has been snowing. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Recent continuous action whose effects are still visible
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect continuous for recent past effects

positives: The roads are wet because it has been raining.
I'm tired because I've been working all day.
negatives: I am working on a new project.
He had been running before the game started.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'yet' to talk about events which are expected to be completed at some point in the future.
example_raw:
[talking about a new mobile phone] I haven't seen it yet . (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

[talking about a book] It's very important because I haven't finished it yet. (Nepal; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Nepali; Pass)

I haven't seen this film yet. (Estonia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Estonian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expectation of a completion in the future

positives: I haven't finished my homework yet.
She has not seen the new movie yet.
negatives: I didn't see the movie yet.
I did not see that one.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'for' to talk about a past event or action which hasn't occurred again in the period of time up to now.
example_raw:
I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time. (Ecuador; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I'm sorry I haven't written for so long. (Greece; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

I haven't seen you for ages. (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Russian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Absence of an action over a period of time

positives: I haven't eaten pizza for a month.
We haven't met for ages.
negatives: I didn't see it yet.
I have lived here for a long time.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form 'have' + '-ed' with pronouns 'I' and 'we', and with a limited range of verbs.
example_raw:
I have seen the Eiffel Tower and many old buildings. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Turkish; Pass)

I like Japanese people and I've been to Japan more than three times. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

We have seen the Tower of London, Big Ben, the Houses of the Parliament and of course Buckingham Palace. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; French; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Reporting a past experience with present relevance
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Affirmative present perfect simple with I and We

positives: I have visited the museum several times.
We've completed the project.
negatives: They have been to the museum.
I hadn't seen the movie.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form 'haven't' + '-ed' with 'I' with a limited range of verbs.
example_raw:
I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time. (Ecuador; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I haven't seen you for a long time. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Hungarian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Denying a past experience up to the present

positives: I haven't tried Italian food.
I have not seen that episode.
negatives: We haven't been there.
He hasn't called me.

can_do_statement: Can use the question form 'have you' + '-ed' with with a limited range of verbs.
example_raw:
Have you bought anything? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

Hi Jools, How have you been? (Japan; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Japanese; Pass)

Where have you been? (Ecuador; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

positives: Have you finished your dinner?
Where have you been all day?
negatives: Have they seen the show?
Do you have a pet?

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect simple with 'already' to emphasise that something is done, often before the expected time.  ► adverbs
example_raw:
I've already planned the party, bought his present, and most important of all, I 've already told everyone. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I have already bought a new arm-chair, yellow and comfortable. (Sweden; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Swedish; Pass)

In Spain lots of universities have already accepted this plan.. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Other; Pass)

So we decided to go to Farhang cinema tonight and we have already bought the tickets. (Iran; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Farsi; Pass)

She has already won three gold medals at international tournaments. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Italian; Fail)

positives: I have already planned the trip.
She has already spoken to the manager.
negatives: I will already be there.
They haven't done it yet.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative forms with a range of pronouns and nouns and an increasing range of verbs.
example_raw:
I've left some clothes at the dry cleaner's 100 yards from my home, in Park Street. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Mandarin; Pass)

It's been an amazing week for me. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

She is from California, but she has just moved to Italy. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Italian; Pass)

Our company has signed deals with a few German companies. (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Panjabi; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Reporting positive past events connected to present state

positives: She has signed the contract.
We've moved to a new city.
negatives: I haven't signed anything.
He has never seen snow.

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect simple with a limited range of adverbs in the normal mid position.
example_raw:
I have never seen a competition like that before, and I love it. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

I have just seen your notice. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Present perfect simple with mid-position adverbs

positives: I have never visited the museum.
She has just left the building.
negatives: I have already seen it.
They haven't finished it.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative forms with a range of pronouns and an increasing range of verbs.
example_raw:
He hasn't spoken to anyone from that time till now. (Iran; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Farsi; Pass)

She is a quiet person so she has not made a lot of friends. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Chinese; Pass)

We haven't decided where to go yet, but probably it will be to somewhere like Australia or New Zealand. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Denial of past events connected to present

positives: He hasn't spoken to anyone.
We have not decided where to go.
negatives: I have decided already.
They didn't go to the park.

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect simple with 'since' to talk about duration.
example_raw:
I have been here since August 2006. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; French; Pass)

It's been a long time since we went out together so I think we will have a great time at the park playing sports and chatting! (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

Many things have changed since your last visit. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

Such a long time has passed since the last time we met. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Marking the starting point of a continuous state

positives: I have lived here since 2005.
It's been a long time since we met.
negatives: I lived here since I was born.
She was working there.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative question form.
example_raw:
Haven't you seen it yet? (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Haven't your parents given you their advice? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Seeking confirmation of an expected event

positives: Haven't you seen the new update?
Hasn't he given you the money?
negatives: Have you seen the new update?
Why haven't they left yet?

can_do_statement: Can use the present perfect simple to talk about experiences up to now.
example_raw:
I've seen the British Museum. (Taiwan; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Chinese; Pass)

We have visited the Coliseum and several museums. (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Armenian; Pass)

After the film, we should go to "The Golden Pagoda" because I've never been there. (Myanmar; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Burmese; Pass)

You know I haven't been to France before. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Hungarian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Stating life experiences without a specific time

positives: I have visited the Coliseum.
She has never been to France.
negatives: I am going to the British Museum.
He went to the museum yesterday.
